name: Do you need a geotechnical report before building a custom home on a hillside lot?

mainEntity.name: Do you need a geotechnical report before building a custom home on a hillside lot in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Do you need a geotechnical report before building a custom home on a hillside lot in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, hillside custom homes in Los Angeles generally need a geotechnical report because the soil and slope conditions directly affect design, safety, and permitting. The report helps identify bearing capacity, drainage issues, slope stability, expansive soils, and the type of foundation system required. On hillside lots, the findings can determine whether the home needs caissons, deeper footings, retaining walls, or drainage improvements. Skipping this step can lead to expensive redesigns or permit delays later. A geotechnical report is most useful early in the process, before finalizing architecture and structural engineering, so the design team can build around the site conditions instead of reacting to them. Homeowners should also make sure the builder and engineer review the report together. If the lot has visible slope, past movement, or poor drainage, the soil work becomes even more important. For LA properties, hillside due diligence is not optional if the goal is to avoid structural surprises and budget blowouts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, hillside custom homes typically need a geotechnical report because soil stability, slope movement, drainage, and foundation design must be evaluated before permits and structural plans are finalized.
